package.title: Bitcoin's Expected Return: An Age Rule That Beats Current Practice
package.data_as_of: Monthly prices to September 2026 for Bitcoin, gold and the S&P 500; to April 2026 for Ether and the address counts. Data accessed 31 October to 3 November 2026.
package.units: In the result tables, rates, returns and misses are fractions a year (0.32 is 32% a year) and shares are fractions of the periods (0.95 is 95%). The column `today` is in per cent. The headline list converts to per cent and says so.

licence.condition: Reuse of the results is allowed with credit to the paper.
licence.third_party_data: The Bitcoin and Ether reference prices and address counts in data/cm_btc.csv and data/cm_eth.csv are from the Coin Metrics community data, licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial use, with attribution). The other inputs are from Bitstamp candles, the World Bank, Robert Shiller's data and FRED. Third-party data keep their own terms and are not covered by the licence above.

package.cite_as: Papadogiannis, A. (2026). Bitcoin's Expected Return: An Age Rule That Beats Current Practice. Working paper. https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7705438
package.cite_package: Papadogiannis, A. (2026). Bitcoin's Expected Return: An Age Rule That Beats Current Practice. Replication package, version 1.1.0. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24004326
package.describe_as: Papadogiannis (2026), "Bitcoin's Expected Return: An Age Rule That Beats Current Practice", working paper, with its replication package.

headline.what: Age-rule forecast of Bitcoin's return, September 2026 to September 2031
headline.unit: per cent a year, compounded over the five years

headline.what: Bitcoin's power-law exponent, estimated in September 2026
headline.unit: (a number; the age rule divides it by Bitcoin's age in years)

headline.what: Share of five-year periods in which Bitcoin beat a fixed rate of 10% a year
Share of five-year periods in which Bitcoin beat the age rule's forecast
Average miss of the age rule over five-year periods
headline.unit: per cent a year, as (1 + realized) / (1 + forecast) - 1, positive if the realized return was higher

headline.what: Average miss of a fixed 10% rate over five-year periods
headline.unit: per cent a year, as (1 + realized) / (1 + rate) - 1, positive if the realized return was higher

headline.what: CAPM required return on Bitcoin, beta over 2012 to 2026, equity premium 4%
CAPM required return on Bitcoin, beta over the last four years, equity premium 4%

tables.what: The backtest for Bitcoin and Ether: the record of each rate at horizons of 3, 4 and 5 years. The age rule appears here as "Power-law trend, fitted to date".

columns.rate: the way of setting the expected return
columns.median: median across periods of the annual miss, a fraction
columns.avg: average across periods of the growth ratio over the horizon, annualised, less one
columns.avg_trim: the same leaving out the largest 5% of the ratios
columns.beat: share of periods in which the realized return exceeded the rate

tables.what: What each method sets as Bitcoin's rate in September 2026, beside its record at 3, 4 and 5 years.

columns.method: the way of setting the expected return
columns.today: the rate it gives in September 2026, in per cent (text; a range where it differs by horizon)
columns.avg3: average miss at 3 years, as `avg` above
columns.beat3: share of 3-year periods in which the rate was beaten
columns.beat4: share of 4-year periods in which the rate was beaten
columns.beat5: share of 5-year periods in which the rate was beaten

tables.what: The same record as ranges across the three horizons, as printed in the paper's table.
The age rule month by month from August 2013: the exponent estimated from data to that month and the rates it implies.

columns.beta: the power-law exponent estimated from data to that month
columns.inst: the instantaneous yearly rate, exp(beta / age) - 1
columns.h5: the yearly rate over the next five years, (1 + 5 / age)^(beta / 5) - 1
columns.h3: the yearly rate over the next three years, (1 + 3 / age)^(beta / 3) - 1

tables.what: Exhibit 2: the exponent, the five-year forecast and the five-year return that followed, by month.

columns.beta: the exponent estimated from data to that month; empty before there is enough data
columns.agerule_5y: the age rule's yearly rate for the next five years
columns.realized_5y: the yearly return over the five years that followed; empty where they have not passed
columns.cagr_since_2012: Bitcoin's compound annual return from January 2012 to that month

tables.what: Average miss of each rate with 95% bands from a stationary block bootstrap, for Bitcoin, Ether and gold.

columns.sample_from: first start month of the periods
columns.rate: the way of setting the expected return
columns.lo: lower end of the 95% band, mean block length 12h months
columns.lo_L2: lower end with mean block length 24h months, as a check
columns.hi_L2: upper end with that block length
columns.beat: share of periods in which the rate was beaten
columns.rate_now: the last value of the rate in the series used for the backtest, a fraction a year; not necessarily the rate today

tables.what: CAPM required returns for Bitcoin, Ether and gold, by sample.

columns.beta: beta of monthly returns on the S&P 500 total-return index
columns.lo: lower end of the 95% interval of beta, Newey-West standard errors
columns.rf: the ten-year Treasury yield at the end of the sample, a fraction
columns.req_erp4: required return with an equity premium of 4%: rf + beta x 0.04
columns.req_erp6: the same with an equity premium of 6%
columns.req_erp4_lo: with the lower end of beta and a premium of 4%
columns.req_erp6_hi: with the upper end of beta and a premium of 6%

tables.what: The record of the age rule and the alternatives in periods beginning January 2020 or later, after the power law was published.

columns.rate: the way of setting the expected return
columns.beat: share of periods in which the rate was beaten

tables.what: The same backtest for gold, with samples from 1981 and from 2012.
The record of every rule for Ether at horizons of 3 to 5 years.
Volatility of each asset, and the share of periods in which a correctly set expected return would be beaten under lognormal returns.

columns.sigma: annualised volatility of monthly log returns, a fraction
columns.beat_h3: share of 3-year periods in which a correctly set expected return would be beaten
columns.mean_over_median_pa: how far the mean yearly return lies above the median, a fraction a year
